**Built this iteration:** closed a real race condition in the submission flow, not just a cosmetic gap. Re-reading `useOfferSubmission`'s reducer, I found that dismissing `CheckoutSheet` mid-`checkoutProcessing` doesn't actually cancel anything — the in-flight `process()` promise still resolves ~600ms later and forces the reducer to `success`/`failure` regardless of what the user did in the meantime. Since `HomeExperience`'s effect watches `submission.state === 'success'` independently of which sheet is open, that means a visitor could dismiss the checkout sheet thinking they backed out, and their offer would still silently land on the public leaderboard with nobody ever seeing a confirmation screen — a real "the UI's model of what happened diverges from what the user believes happened" bug, not just an edge case.

Fixed it at the root rather than patching the reducer: added a `dismissible` prop to `Sheet.tsx` (defaults `true`, keeps focus-trap/Tab-wrapping active regardless) that makes Escape and backdrop-click inert. `CheckoutSheet` now passes `dismissible={!isProcessing}`, so there's no way to close the sheet at all during the one window where doing so would be misleading — the race can't happen through the UI anymore, not just "happens less often." Added a small "can't be interrupted once it's started" status line so the disabled state has a stated reason, not just a silently unresponsive Escape key.

**Tests:** extended `tests/components/Sheet.test.tsx` with a `dismissible={false}` block (Escape ignored, backdrop-click ignored, focus trap still works), and added `tests/components/CheckoutSheet.test.tsx` verifying the actual state→dismissible mapping end to end (blocked during `checkoutProcessing`, allowed in `disclaimerAck`/`failure`/`success`).
